claim: >-

  normalized-value implementation is admissible. Public names, production
  dependency adapters, package carriers, raw carrier exposure, and repeated
  binding-record semantics remain private or excluded pending their respective
  accepted decisions. Two P1 issues remain: the owner-start precondition is not
  enforced, and the proposed raw boundary does not define safe behavior for a
  proxied invocation wrapper.

findings:
  - severity: P1
    location: >-
      docs/decisions/0015-block-publication-surfaces-and-runtime-claims-while-decisions-stay-open.md:108-113;
      docs/architecture/mvp-implementation-roadmap.md:125-134;
      architecture/checks/production-artifacts.mjs:107-140;
      architecture/checks/governance.mjs:178-201,698-707;
      tests/governance.test.mjs:401-422
    reproduction: |-
      Command:
      node --input-type=module -e 'import {productionArtifactsBlockedByOpenDecisions} from "./architecture/checks/production-artifacts.mjs";const x=await productionArtifactsBlockedByOpenDecisions(["packages/core/package.json","packages/core/src/features/compiler/normalized-compiler.ts"],{readPackageManifest:async()=>({name:"@get-modular/core",private:true})});process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify({blocked:x})+"\n")'

      Observed:
      {"blocked":[]}

      ADR-0015 requires a governed product-owner start decision before the first
      production source. The roadmap additionally requires the admission checker
      to consume that record. Neither classifier nor validateBlockedImplementation
      accepts or verifies such a record, and the existing positive test explicitly
      admits private source without one.
    minimalCorrection: >-
      Make a governed, product-owner-approved start record a mandatory input to
      first-production-package admission. Verify its repository, authorized base
      SHA, package identity, owner, and private normalized-semantics scope. Add a
      negative test proving otherwise-valid private source fails when that record
      is missing, stale, mismatched, or broader than M1.
    productOwnerDecisionRequired: false
  - severity: P1
    location: >-
      docs/decisions/0006-clarify-v1-compiler-normalization-and-entry-points.md:64-74;
      docs/open-decisions/OD-005-raw-input-carrier-semantics.md:20-26,58-62;
      docs/decisions/0013-close-trusted-object-and-raw-carrier-semantics.md:128-132,177-182,261-278
    reproduction: |-
      Command:
      node --input-type=module -e 'let traps=0;const wrapper=new Proxy({}, {getOwnPropertyDescriptor(){traps++;throw new Error("wrapper-trap")}});try{Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(wrapper,"declarations")}catch(e){process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify({trapCount:traps,error:e.message})+"\n")}'

      Observed:
      {"trapCount":1,"error":"wrapper-trap"}

      OD-005 expressly includes the top-level invocation record and directs
      possibly proxied values to the raw entrypoint. ADR-0013 reads that wrapper
      with Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor. The proposal defines safe intrinsic
      classification for individual Uint8Array carriers but does not say whether
      the wrapper and declaration list must be trusted, nor how wrapper Proxy
      traps are contained or mapped. A trap can execute arbitrary caller code,
      throw, or fail to terminate before byte classification.
    minimalCorrection: >-
      Before ADR-0013 acceptance, explicitly choose and specify the trust boundary.
      Either require the host to construct a trusted ordinary wrapper and dense
      declaration array, limiting the phrase "untrusted byte boundary" to carrier
      contents, or redesign the invocation contract. Add ordinary, proxied,
      revoked-proxy, throwing-trap, and nonterminating-trap cases with exact
      disposition; do not claim trap-free hostile-wrapper handling that JavaScript
      cannot provide.
    productOwnerDecisionRequired: true

  - "Does the owner-start record bind the pre-implementation authorization base SHA or another source identity? The checker needs one non-self-referential rule."
  - "Should pre-ADR-0009 src/index.ts absence remain review-only, or become a mechanical private-boundary check?"

recommendedDecision: >-
  NO-GO for first-source admission under the current checker and NO-GO for
  accepting ADR-0013 as written. After enforcing the owner-start record, a
  CONDITIONAL GO is supportable only for private M1 normalized-value semantics
  with owned primitives. Keep all public names, production external adapters,
  package carriers, raw exposure, and repeated-record behavior gated until their
  corresponding decisions and evidence are accepted.
